Classes

CellBuffer

A grid of cells plus a cursor position. All writes clip to the buffer and keep wide glyphs consistent: a wide glyph always owns a continuation cell, and overwriting either half blanks the other.

Text writes (Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetString(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Char},Tuinet.Style,System.Int32,Tuinet.Overflow), Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetRune(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Text.Rune,Tuinet.Style)) layer: a default foreground or background in the style keeps the color already in the cell, so text drawn on a filled panel keeps the panel's background. Attributes are replaced. Tuinet.CellBuffer.Fill(Tuinet.Rect,Tuinet.Style) and Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetCell(System.Int32,System.Int32,Tuinet.Cell) replace whole cells.

Fuzzy

Fuzzy matching for filtering lists by what was typed (a command palette, a file picker): the pattern's chars must appear in the text in order, not necessarily together. Higher scores are better matches. Allocation-free, O(n).

InlineOptions

Inline mode: instead of the alternate screen, draw a live band of Tuinet.InlineOptions.Height rows under the shell prompt. The band stays in the terminal (and its scrollback) after exit.

Layout

Splits a rect along one axis. Allocation-free: constraints come in as a span (a collection expression stays on the stack) and results go into a caller-provided span.

Span<Rect> rows = stackalloc Rect[3];
Layout.Vertical(area, [Constraint.Length(1), Constraint.Fill(), Constraint.Length(1)], rows);
Markup

A small markup for styled text, parsed into caller memory without allocating.

  • [b] bold, [dim], [i] italic, [u] underline, [blink], [reverse], [hidden], [s] strike (long names work too: [bold], [italic], …).
  • [fg=red], [bg=#1C2433]: a name (black … white, bright-red …, default), #RRGGBB, or a palette index 0–255. A bare color name or #RRGGBB sets the foreground; a bare number is just text.
  • Several in one tag: [b fg=#F5A623]. [/] closes the latest tag.
  • [[ is a literal [. A tag that doesn't parse is kept as text, so [1/3] needs no escaping.
Terminal

An immediate-mode terminal session: the alternate screen (or, with Tuinet.TerminalOptions.Inline, a band under the prompt), raw input, double-buffered output.

Single-threaded: call Tuinet.Terminal.Poll(Tuinet.Event@,System.Int32), Tuinet.Terminal.BeginFrame and Tuinet.Terminal.Present from one thread. Tuinet.Terminal.Post(System.Object) may be called from any thread to wake the loop. 

using var term = Terminal.Open();
while (running)
{
    if (!term.Poll(out Event ev, Timeout.Infinite)) continue;
    do { running = app.Handle(ev); } while (running && term.Poll(out ev, 0)); // coalesce bursts
    CellBuffer frame = term.BeginFrame();
    app.Render(frame);
    term.Present();                                                             // one write
}

Or implement Tuinet.IApp and let Tuinet.Terminal.Run(Tuinet.IApp,System.Int32) be that loop.

Structs

Alarm

A one-shot "at this time" check for time-based changes (hide a message after 3 s, debounce a search) without timers or callbacks. Keep it in your state, check it with the loop's time, and return Tuinet.Alarm.DueMs from Tuinet.IApp.NextDueMs(System.Int64) so Tuinet.Terminal.Run(Tuinet.IApp,System.Int32) wakes for it. default is not set.

flashAlarm.Start(nowMs, 3000);                     // when the message is shown
if (flashAlarm.Fire(nowMs)) flash = "";            // in Handle: true once, when due
public long NextDueMs(long nowMs) => flashAlarm.DueMs;
Cell

One terminal cell: glyph, style, display width, hyperlink. Exactly 16 bytes, blittable and canonical, so the renderer compares whole rows with a vectorized memcmp.

Color

A terminal color: the terminal default, a palette index (0-255), or 24-bit RGB. Four bytes, compared bitwise. Downsampled at emit time to the terminal's Tuinet.ColorMode.

Constraint

How much of the split axis one segment gets. See Tuinet.Layout.Split(Tuinet.Rect,Tuinet.Direction,System.ReadOnlySpan{Tuinet.Constraint},System.Span{Tuinet.Rect},System.Int32).

Event

One input event. Only the members matching Tuinet.Event.Kind are meaningful.

FocusRing

Which of Tuinet.FocusRing.Count controls has focus, as an index that wraps around: Tab and Shift+Tab move it, and a click on a control focuses it. A plain value kept in your state; widgets still take Focused = ring.Is(i).

var focus = new FocusRing(3);                        // name, notify, Save
if (ev.Kind == EventKind.Key && focus.Handle(ev.Key)) return;
frame.Render(new Button("Save") { Focused = focus.Is(2) }, saveArea);
KeyEvent

A key press. Printable keys are Tuinet.KeyCode.Char with Tuinet.KeyEvent.Rune set; Ctrl+letter is the lowercase letter with Tuinet.Modifiers.Ctrl. Releases (Tuinet.KeyKind.Release, opt-in) never match Tuinet.KeyEvent.IsChar(System.Char), Tuinet.KeyEvent.IsCtrl(System.Char) or Tuinet.KeyEvent.Is(Tuinet.KeyCode,Tuinet.Modifiers), so key bindings don't fire twice.

MouseEvent

A mouse report (requires Tuinet.TerminalOptions.Mouse). Coordinates are 0-based cells.

Rect

A screen rectangle. Width and height are never negative.

Size
Style

Foreground, background and text attributes. Ten bytes, no padding.

StyledRun

Length chars of a Tuinet.StyledText drawn in Style.

StyledText

Text with several styles: the text, runs that cover it from the start (each run's style is layered over Tuinet.StyledText.Style), and the base style for anything the runs don't cover. A view over caller memory, so it costs nothing to build: runs are typically a collection expression on the stack, or come from a Tuinet.StyledTextBuilder or Tuinet.Markup.Parse(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Char},System.Span{System.Char},System.Span{Tuinet.StyledRun},Tuinet.Style).

buffer.SetText(x, y, new StyledText("j/k move", [new(3, keyStyle), new(5, dimStyle)]));
StyledTextBuilder

Builds a Tuinet.StyledText into caller memory (usually stackalloc), merging adjacent runs with the same style. Never throws when full: what fits is kept and Tuinet.StyledTextBuilder.Overflowed is set.

var keys = new StyledTextBuilder(stackalloc char[64], stackalloc StyledRun[8]);
keys.Append("j/k", key);
keys.Append(" move  ", dim);
keys.Append(count, key);
buffer.SetText(x, y, keys.Build());

Interfaces

IApp

An app for Tuinet.Terminal.Run(Tuinet.IApp,System.Int32): it handles events and draws frames, and the loop decides when. Times are milliseconds since Tuinet.Terminal.Run(Tuinet.IApp,System.Int32) started.

IStatefulWidget<TState>

A widget whose render reads and updates app-owned state (selection, scroll, caret).

ITty

The platform seam: raw byte I/O with a terminal. Implement it to run a Tuinet.Terminal over anything (a pty, a socket, a test double).

IWidget

An immediate-mode widget: a value describing what to draw, rendered into an area of a buffer. Widgets hold no state between frames; implement them as readonly ref structs so they can carry spans (e.g. stackalloc-formatted text) at zero allocation cost.
